name: Adib Hassan
about:
Adib Hassan has completed his undergraduate (BSc) degree from the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) at Rajshahi University of Engineering & Technology (RUET), Bangladesh. He is an emerging researcher with a strong interest in photonics, metamaterials, and biomedical sensing technologies, particularly in the development and optimization of advanced Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) biosensors for medical diagnostics.

His research focuses on high-sensitivity SPR-based biosensing systems for the detection of infectious diseases. His work involves the design and optimization of highly sensitive prism-based and photonic crystal fiber (PCF)-based SPR sensors using numerical and multiphysics simulation techniques, including Transfer Matrix Method (TMM), Finite Element Method (FEM), MATLAB, and COMSOL Multiphysics. 

Alongside his research activities, he has been actively engaged in academic leadership and professional organizations, taking on several key leadership roles. He served as Chair of the IEEE RUET Student Branch and Vice Chair of the IEEE Computer Society Bangladesh Chapter’s Secretariat Executive Committee, while also serving as Vice Chair of RUET CORE. In addition, he held the position of Director of Hult Prize RUET and served as Secretary of the Notre Dame College Association of RUET. Through these diverse roles, he has contributed to fostering innovation, promoting leadership development, strengthening technical engagement, and advancing student-led initiatives within academic and professional communities.

His broader academic interests include nanophotonics, optical sensing systems, computational electromagnetics, and interdisciplinary biomedical engineering applications. He is particularly motivated by research that bridges fundamental science with practical healthcare solutions, aiming to contribute to the development of affordable and efficient diagnostic technologies.

Adib Hassan aims to pursue an MSc or PhD in a research-intensive environment where he can deepen his expertise in optical biosensing, applied photonics, metamaterials, and related interdisciplinary fields. His long-term goal is to contribute to impactful innovations in biomedical diagnostics and advanced sensing technologies through research and development. To support these aspirations, he is particularly interested in fully funded graduate opportunities that offer Graduate Research Assistantships (GRA) or Teaching Assistantships (TA), enabling him to advance his academic and research career while contributing to ongoing research initiatives.
